name: 16b segment recurrence
title: Segment recurrence carrying one fact across segments
subtitle: Two layers, three-token segments, memory holds the previous segment from the layer below; toy attention averages what it sees

steps.caption: Token 1 carries the value 9, standing for a debt figure, and every other token carries 0. Each layer averages everything it can see: the earlier tokens of its own segment plus the memory of the segment before.
Segment 1 has no memory. Layer 1 gives 9, 4.5 and 3, and layer 2 averages those into 9, 6.75 and 5.5. The input and layer 1 states of tokens 1 to 3 are stored as memory with no gradient path.
Segment 2 reads that memory. Layer 1 gives 2.25, 1.8 and 1.5, and layer 2 gives 4.69, 4.11 and 3.68. Without memory every state in this segment would be 0.
In segment 3 the input memory holds only zeros, so layer 1 gives 0, 0 and 0. Layer 2 still reads layer 1 of segment 2 and gives 1.39, 1.11 and 0.93, so the fact survives one level up.
In segment 4 both memories hold zeros and the fact is gone. Two layers carried it two segments forward, about one extra segment per layer, and each hop diluted it.
At real scale, 32 layers and 512-token segments reach back about 16,384 tokens. Each query scores 1,024 keys, its own segment plus memory, while gradients stay inside the current segment.
